messages.author: af72d10915854c2f
messages.subject: Displaying reactive events
parts: Is anyone familiar with the code to enable the graphical display of reactive events?  I used this once but lost the information.  Basically, a when running a shiny app it allowed a control key to display the realtime creation of object by shiny based on reactive events.

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Displaying reactive events
parts:
See ?shiny::showReactLog

To quote the doc:

> To use the reactive log visualizer, start with a fresh R session and run the commandoptions(shiny.reactlog=TRUE); then launch your application in the usual way (e.g. using runApp). At any time you can hit Ctrl+F3 (or for Mac users, Command+F3) in your web browser to launch the reactive log visualization.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Displaying reactive events
parts: You'd have to put options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE) at the top of your server.R or in a global.R file if you want it to work when deployed. But if you're expecting a lot of traffic for your app, I don't recommend it--the reactlog only grows in size, it never shrinks, and also adds runtime overhead to every reactive computation. Best to use it for testing then re-deploy with it disabled.
